candidates.statement: D. This SOPP does not: • Describe the criteria for determining whether a postmarketing study or clinical trial should be a PMR or a PMC;
candidates.context: • PMRs for deferred pediatric studies under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) • Agreed-upon, reportable 506B PMCs; and • Agreed-upon non-506B commitments (i.e., PMC for Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) and certain product stability studies). • Describe the criteria for determining non-compliance with the conduct of PMRs or the required reporting for PMRs/PMCs;

candidates.statement: 1. Accelerated approval confirmatory studies (21 CFR 314.510/Subpart H and 601.41/Subpart E), where subsequent studies are required to describe and verify clinical benefit.
candidates.context: A. In the past, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) used the term “postmarketing study commitments (PMCs)” to refer to studies or clinical trials conducted by the applicant after FDA approved or licensed a product for marketing. These studies, or clinical trials, were intended to further refine the safety, efficacy or optimal use of a product or to ensure consistency and reliability of product quality. These commitments were either agreed upon by the FDA and the applicant or required by FDA in the following situations: 2. Deferred pediatric studies (21 CFR 314.55(b) and 601.27(b)), where studies are required under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) NOTE: Reference to PREA related PMRs are included to maintain background completeness.

candidates.statement: A. 506B-Reportable Postmarketing Commitment (506B PMC) – Postmarketing studies or clinical trials concerning clinical safety, clinical efficacy, clinical pharmacology, or nonclinical toxicology that applicants and the FDA have agreed, in writing, to conduct; and applicants are required to report on these PMCs in their PMR/PMC annual report (21 CFR 314.81(b)(2)(vii)(a), 21 CFR 601.70(b), and Section 506B the FD&C Act, Reports of Postmarketing Studies).
candidates.context: B. Clinical Trial – Any prospective investigation in which an applicant or investigator determines the method of assigning the investigational product or other interventions to one or more human subjects.

candidates.statement: F. Postmarketing Requirement (PMR) – Any study or clinical trial that an applicant is required to conduct post-approval of a marketing application or a supplement. NOTE: Applicants may be subject to legal penalties for not conducting PMRs.
candidates.context: E. Postmarketing Commitment (PMC) – Any study or clinical trial that an applicant has agreed upon, in writing, to conduct after approval or licensing of a marketing application or supplement that is not a PMR. G. CBER Sentinel Sufficiency Assessment – Under section 901 of FDAAA, a required determination by CBER of the sufficiency (i.e. capability) of CBER Sentinel to further characterize serious risk(s) of concern. Sentinel insufficiency serves as a justification for whether a Title IX PMR is warranted.

candidates.statement: J. “Safety-related” Study (Title IX PMR under FDAAA or 506B safety-related PMC) - A study being conducted specifically to evaluate safety or further investigate a safety issue(s) associated with a product. NOTE: A study must have a primary safety endpoint to be considered a safety-related study.
candidates.context: I. Voluntary Postmarketing Study or Trial – A study or clinical trial conducted on an applicant’s own initiative without a formal request by FDA (i.e., not in an FDA letter). K. “Safety-related Product Quality Study” (Title IX PMR under FDAAA) - A quality (CMC) study conducted specifically to address unresolved product quality issues related to the risk of a serious adverse drug experience under FDAAA. NOTE: A study must have a primary endpoint related to product quality safety to be considered a safety-related product quality study. For example, in order to identify a serious risk of patient exposure to a virus and subsequent viral infection, a safety-related product quality study may be required to demonstrate clearance or inactivation of viruses.

NOTE: A study must have a primary endpoint related to product quality safety to be considered a safety-related product quality study. For example, in order to identify a serious risk of patient exposure to a virus and subsequent viral infection, a safety-related product quality study may be required to demonstrate clearance or inactivation of viruses.

candidates.statement: Q2. What should you consider when developing a non-506B PMC? A2 . There are a number of issues to consider:
candidates.context: Questions: Q1. What is a non-506B PMC? A1 . A Non-Reportable Postmarketing Commitment (non-506B PMC) is any study to assess drug or biologic product quality that is not required for approval; yet, the review committee deems necessary to provide complete quality information. A non-506B PMC is concurred, in writing, by the applicant and FDA. Studies may include manufacturing, stability, and other studies that do not have primary safety as an endpoint. 1. Is the generation of the non-506B PMC based on a risk/benefit model? If the incomplete information is critical to “approving” an application or supplement and cannot be obtained and reviewed within the review cycle, the review committee should not approve the application or supplement but should, instead issue a Complete Response (CR) letter.
